latin.424: §. V. At verò, vix ac ne vix quidem salutare hoc verboque Dei exactè congruum Judicium Patrum Constantinopolitanorum, cum subnixa ratione suâ haud indecedente, exauditum fuerat, cum imaginum Patroni graviter illi irascerentur ac inviderent, donec, elapsis præter propter annis 30. ira eorum ac indignatio ita cresceret, ut alio in Concilio, Nicææ habito, & ab hac Civitate Nicænum secundum dicto, ab idololatris Pontificiis verò, haud secus ac Constantinopolitanum ab Orthodoxis, Oecumenicum septimum nuncupato, Patribus Constantinopolitanis Decreto adversô contradictum fuerit.
latin.425: Sequenti modô: Imaginum usum cultumque in templis haud aspernandum esse, in specie Christi imagines crucifixi pro nobis, memoriam ejus resuscitare.
latin.426: Rationem verò in contrarium, ab Eucharistiæ imagine & figura petitam, usque adeo falsam esse, ut censendum omnino sit, panem consecratum in S. Coena neutiquam Figuram corporis Christi, sed ipsum potius corpus Christi existere.
latin.427: Hoc tamen ipsum, cum propriè accipi non posset, panis substantia, à substantia corporis Christi, totâ specie diversa remanente, nec uno disparatorum integro residuôque, alterius naturam essentiamque specificam participaturo, Conversionem panis in corpus Christi implicitè insinuabat, i. e. Transsubstantiationis pullum, ovi cortice, ceu involucro suo, obtectum, fovebat, mox fractô cortice lucem adspecturum postque octiduum quasi circumcidendum etiam, nomineque proprio insigniendum.
latin.428: Ab eo tempore, puta à tempore habiti Concilii Niceni secundi, non certe citius (sunt verba Bellarmini) GRÆCI PATRES SÆPE, (non tamen semper) MONUERUNT, (non verò expressè inculcarunt) EUCHARISTIAM NON ESSE FIGURAM, SED CORPUS CHRISTI, Tom. 3. de Eucharist. p. m. 579. Ingolstad. edit. Modum interim, quô Eucharistia corpus Christi esset, per 200. circiter annos, in totum adhuc ignorabant inque medio relinquebant.
latin.429: Usque dum Seculo demum IX. exurgeret præced. annot. memoratus Paschasius Rhadebertus, Bertramum, panem Eucharisticum cum Veteribus, etiam Figuram corporis Christi contendentem, oppugnaturus, assertis autem hujusmodi, decertans, quæ Conversionem panis in corpus Christi, disertè profitebantur: e.g. cùm diceret: Sub specie panis visibilis, nihil aliud quam caro Christi porrigitur. Item: Panis in carnem, & vinum in sanguinem convertitur. lib. de corpore & sang. domini, cap. 10. & 20., allegante Francisco Foris Otrokocsi in Irenico cap. 6. §. 1. p. m. 69. ac sequenti modô in posteriorem Paschasii propositionem commentante: Scil. de crassiusculâ & substantiali conversione, ex mente Paschasii, secus quam aliqui veterum atque etiam ipse Bertramus, de sacramenti & mystica locutione & immutatione, locuti sunt nonnulli.
latin.430: Hoc tamen observandum de Paschasio, quòd etsi propriè dici nam Christi carnem contendat perpetuò porrigi à Sacerdote sub specie panis & naturalem sanguinem sub specie vini, neget tamen ab ullo quàm A VERO FIDELI percipi carnem & sanguinem: negat etiam ullo modo dentibus vorari carnem Christi, quæ sanè mira sunt, atque in his multum differt ipse à posteris suæ sententiæ sequacibus. Contenderet manibus tractari carnem Christi, eamque sub specie panis, in os mitti, NON tamen DENTIBUS ATTERI. Scilicet, nondum ille subtilitatem figmenti tunc adhuc recentis tâm operosè edisseruit, sicut Lombardus, aliique post ipsum de Solorum Accidentium fractione & attritione. Hucusque Otrokocsi dicto loco.

pass_a.424: §. V. But scarcely, nay hardly at all, had this salutary Judgment of the Constantinopolitan Fathers, exactly congruent with the Word of God, with its supporting reason not departing, been heard, when the Patrons of images were gravely angry at them and envious, until, about 30 years having elapsed, their wrath and indignation so grew that in another Council held at Nicaea, and from that City called the Second Nicene — but by idolatrous Pontiffs named the Seventh Oecumenical no less than the Constantinopolitan by the Orthodox — it was contradicted to the Constantinopolitan Fathers by an adverse Decree.
pass_a.425: In the following manner: that the use and cult of images in temples is by no means to be despised; in particular images of Christ crucified for us revive His memory.
pass_a.426: But the reason to the contrary, drawn from the image and figure of the Eucharist, [was declared] so false that it is to be judged altogether that the bread consecrated in the Holy Supper is by no means a Figure of Christ’s body, but rather exists as Christ’s body itself.
pass_a.427: Yet this very thing, since it could not be taken properly — the substance of bread remaining diverse in whole species from the substance of Christ’s body, and neither of the disparates, whole and residual, about to participate the specific nature and essence of the other — implicitly insinuated a Conversion of bread into Christ’s body, i.e. fostered Transsubstantiation’s chick covered by the egg’s shell as by its wrapper, soon, the shell broken, about to look upon the light and after an octave as it were also to be circumcised and marked with its proper name.
pass_a.428: From that time, namely from the time of the Second Nicene Council held, not certainly sooner (Bellarmine’s words) the GREEK FATHERS OFTEN (yet not always) WARNED (but did not expressly inculcate) that the EUCHARIST IS NOT A FIGURE, BUT THE BODY OF CHRIST, Tom. 3 de Eucharist. p. 579 Ingolstadt ed. Meanwhile the mode by which the Eucharist would be Christ’s body they still for about 200 years altogether ignored and left in the middle.
pass_a.429: Until at last in the ninth Century there arose Paschasius Radbertus, remembered in the preceding annotation, about to oppose Bertram, who with the Ancients contended that the Eucharistic bread is also a Figure of Christ’s body, and contending with assertions of this sort which expressly professed a Conversion of bread into Christ’s body: e.g. when he said: Under the visible species of bread nothing other than Christ’s flesh is offered. Likewise: Bread is converted into flesh, and wine into blood. Lib. de corpore & sang. Domini, ch. 10 & 20, alleged by Francis Foris Otrokocsi in the Irenicum ch. 6 §. 1 p. 69, and commenting on Paschasius’s latter proposition thus: Namely of a somewhat crasser and substantial conversion, in Paschasius’s mind, otherwise than some of the ancients and Bertram himself spoke of sacramental and mystic speech and immutation.
pass_a.430: Yet this is to be observed of Paschasius: that although he contends Christ’s flesh is properly said to be perpetually offered by the Priest under the species of bread and natural blood under the species of wine, he yet denies flesh and blood are perceived by any except A TRUE BELIEVER; he also denies Christ’s flesh is in any way chewed by teeth — which are indeed marvelous things, and in these he differs much from later followers of his sentence. He would contend Christ’s flesh is handled by hands and under the species of bread put into the mouth, yet NOT WORN AWAY BY TEETH. Clearly he had not yet so laboriously expounded the subtlety of a fiction then still recent, as Lombard and others after him on the fraction and attrition of Accidents alone. Thus far Otrokocsi in the said place.

424: §.V: the Constantinopolitans’ salutary, Word-congruent judgment was barely heard before image-patrons grew angry.

After ~30 years their indignation forced Nicaea II — called Second Nicene from the city, but by pontiffs ‘Seventh Oecumenical’ (as the Orthodox had styled Constantinopolitanum) — and an adverse decree contradicted those Fathers.
425: Nicaea II: temple image use and cult are not to be despised.
In particular, images of Christ crucified for us revive His memory.
426: The counter-reason from the Eucharist as image/figure was judged so false that consecrated supper-bread must be held not a Figure of Christ’s body but the body itself.
427: Taken properly that cannot stand: bread’s substance remains wholly diverse in species from Christ’s body, and neither disparate shares the other’s specific essence.
So it implicitly fostered Conversion — Transsubstantiation’s chick under the egg-shell, soon to break into light and after an octave be named.
428: Bellarmine: from Nicaea II (not sooner) Greek Fathers often — not always — warned the Eucharist is not a figure but Christ’s body (Tom. 3 de Eucharist. p. 579 Ingolstadt); they did not expressly inculcate it.
For ~200 years they still left the mode wholly unknown, in the middle.
429: Ninth century: Paschasius Radbertus rises against Bertram (who with the Ancients kept the bread a Figure) and expressly professes conversion — under visible bread-species only Christ’s flesh is offered; bread into flesh, wine into blood (De corp. & sang. Dom. 10 & 20).
Otrokocsi: Paschasius means a crasser substantial conversion, unlike ancients/Bertram’s sacramental-mystic speech.
430: Paschasius quirks: flesh and blood under the species, yet received only by a true believer; not chewed by teeth — marvels that already distance him from later followers.
Hands may handle and mouth receive under bread-species, but teeth do not wear the flesh; he had not yet spun Lombard’s accident-only fraction/attrition subtlety. Hucusque Otrokocsi.
